inputs.original_text: Organisers of the “No Kings” protests claim 8 million people attended more than 3,300 events across all 50 states, but authorities have provided no official count. That is a sizeable claim from the people promoting the demonstrations, not proof of a national consensus. Organisers say turnout was about one million higher, with 600 more events, than at the last demonstrations in October. Even so, noisy rallies are not a substitute for lawful authority or a mandate from the whole country. A nation cannot be governed by whichever political faction can organize the biggest protest.
inputs.modified_text: The organizers say 8 million people attended more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states, and claim turnout was about one million higher than in October. But there is no official count, and a movement’s own figures are not proof that the country agrees with it. These rallies are political pressure campaigns, not a substitute for lawful authority or the consent of the nation. A country governed by law and tradition cannot be run by whichever faction can stage the loudest protest.
